title: Stale line citation in patterns.md:909 -- cites test/dispatch.test.ts:769 but the assertion is at :778
description:
Shipped defect in CAM-376 (PR #301, v0.225.0), confirmed on main after merge.

The US-R1-002 bullet at scripts/cam/patterns.md:909 cites `test/dispatch.test.ts:769` as the location of the `recordedSleeps.every(...)` assertion. MEASURED on main: that assertion is at test/dispatch.test.ts:778, and line 769 is a comment line. The citation was already off by 9 when written, in the very commit that added the bullet (2183fbf2).

This matters more than a normal typo: US-002's pinning oracle in that same PRD exists precisely to protect absolute line-number cross-references in patterns.md from rot, and patterns.md bullets cross-reference each other by absolute line number throughout. A wrong pointer in the knowledge layer sends the next reader to a comment line.

The sibling citations in the same bullet are CORRECT and must not be touched: src/tmux/dispatch.ts:544 is genuinely `retryBaseMs = 300`, and test/dispatch.test.ts:754 is correct as a HISTORICAL main-referencing citation (the pre-fix location), not a live pointer.

SCOPE: change :769 to :778 in the bullet at patterns.md:909. Verify the two sibling citations still resolve before committing. Doc-only, NO rebuild.

ORACLE NOTE for whoever specs this: do NOT freeze 778 as a literal comparand -- derive it (`grep -n 'recordedSleeps.every' test/dispatch.test.ts`), per the derive-don't-freeze rule that PR #301 itself shipped at patterns.md:903. Do NOT target scripts/cam/handoff.json as an evidence oracle, per patterns.md:907. Both rules were violated by the CAM-376 PRD's own criteria and cost that cycle all three review rounds.

spec.scope: Doc-only fix to scripts/cam/patterns.md. The US-R1-002 bullet (CAM-376 review round 1) cites the recordedSleeps.every assertion by a stale absolute line number, test/dispatch.test.ts:769. That token points at a comment line on main; the live assertion is at 777 and drifts every time the test file changes above it (the issue's own proposed :778 was already stale on arrival too). Root-cause fix per the repo's own precedent at patterns.md:913 and the derive-don't-freeze rule at patterns.md:903: drop the :769 line-number suffix and let the pointer anchor on the assertion's content, which the bullet already quotes inline (recordedSleeps.every((ms) => ms === POLL_INTERVAL_MS)). This makes the citation rot-proof (grep-able content reference, never a line number that rots). NON-GOALS: do not touch the sibling US-003 bullet or any of its citations (its stale test/dispatch.test.ts:754 is a separately-tracked defect, out of scope); do not introduce any new absolute line number for this pointer; do not edit any code or test file. Doc-only, NO rebuild (patterns.md is not sidecar-executed).
acceptanceCriteria: The stale absolute-line citation test/dispatch.test.ts:769 no longer appears anywhere in scripts/cam/patterns.md (the US-R1-002 bullet's pointer to the recordedSleeps.every assertion is now a rot-proof grep-able content reference). [oracle: ! grep -qF 'test/dispatch.test.ts:769' scripts/cam/patterns.md]

The US-R1-002 bullet still anchors its pointer on the assertion's content, so the reference stays resolvable after the line-number suffix is dropped. [oracle: file-assert grep -qF 'recordedSleeps.every((ms) => ms === POLL_INTERVAL_MS)' scripts/cam/patterns.md]

The content reference resolves: the cited recordedSleeps.every assertion genuinely exists in test/dispatch.test.ts. [oracle: file-assert grep -qF 'recordedSleeps.every((ms) => ms === POLL_INTERVAL_MS)' test/dispatch.test.ts]

Only the one stale line-number token changed: the bullet's meaning is preserved, the sibling US-003 bullet and its citations are untouched, and no new absolute line number was introduced for this pointer. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
gotchas: Derive-don't-freeze (patterns.md:903): never re-freeze a new line number; the fix must be a content reference, not :769 changed to another :NNN.
Never target scripts/cam/handoff.json as an evidence oracle (patterns.md:909): it is a rotating artifact. All oracles here target durable surfaces (patterns.md and test/dispatch.test.ts).
Line numbers already drifted: the bullet is at ~line 911 (issue title says 909) and the live assertion is at 777 (issue says 778); do NOT trust any number, grep for content.
Keep it surgical: the sibling US-003 bullet also carries a stale citation (test/dispatch.test.ts:754) but that is out of scope for this issue and must not be touched.
Doc-only edit to a knowledge file: no code change, no rebuild, gates are typecheck/tests unaffected.
domainTerms: patterns.md US-R1-002 bullet: the knowledge-layer entry about vacuous Array#every on empty collections
rot-proof content reference: cite an assertion by its grep-able text instead of an absolute path:NNN line number that drifts
recordedSleeps.every((ms) => ms === POLL_INTERVAL_MS): the assertion the stale pointer names, live in test/dispatch.test.ts
